messages:
sam: heads-up — noticed a regression in batch admission after the staging deploy. OOM spikes when KV cache is near watermark during 512-token bursts. Profiling trace uploaded: /artifacts/prof/trace-2234567890.gz. OOM rate jumped from ~2% -> ~6% on g4-small under mixed traffic.

deploy-bot: Deployed rev abc123 to staging at 2025-02-26T12:34:56Z :rocket:

alex: same here. flamegraph shows kernel fallback to cpu_quant during batch assembly which correlates with heavy KV eviction pressure. Seems the batch token budget is blind to per-request KV footprint.

priya: current logic sets batch_token_budget = 1024 (fixed) for this route. requests with long prefixes carry ~1.0-1.5MB of KV state each (we measured). If multiple such reqs are admitted we hit headroom.

jen: proposal: compute predicted_kv_size(req) from prefix_len + kv_meta, estimate per-request working_set = predicted_kv_size + kernel_estimate(tokens), then admit only while sum(working_set) + reserved_headroom <= device_free_mem. Pseudocode:

```
# called for each incoming request
def should_admit(req, batch):
    req_kv = estimate_kv(req)  # bytes
    req_kernel = kernel_mem_estimate(req.tokens)  # bytes
    predicted_total = batch.kv_sum + batch.kernel_sum + req_kv + req_kernel
    return predicted_total + RESERVED_HEADROOM <= device_free_mem
```

This keeps admission tight to actual footprint rather than just token counts.

sam: we should make it soft-admit first: allow a small overcommit slack and prefer shedding the largest-prefix requests when memory tight. Also add a fallback knob to trigger earlier kernel fallback before eviction churn.

infra-bot: created alert #alerts/kv-admit-oom (severity: high) — fires if OOM rate > 5% on pool g4-staging for 2m.

alex: experiment plan: 1) add lightweight estimate hook to the batcher (+ telemetry), 2) compute per-batch token budget = min(global_token_budget, floor(available_mem / avg_req_working_set)), 3) implement soft-shedding by sorting incoming queue by predicted_kv_size desc, 4) canary to 10% of staging traffic. I'll open PR with benchmarks.

priya: please emit telemetry fields: predicted_kv_sum, batch_token_budget, kernel_choice_hint, admit_decision_reason. Those will make regression debugging much easier.

jen: SGTM. I'll run canary and rollback if OOM > 0.8% sustained over 5m. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
